headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGen can write and execute code while LightZero is read-only, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error exposure only if they are wired together.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest files and stdin/stdout and is a multi-agent orchestration framework; LightZero has no I/O surfaces or write paths. A prompt-injection bridge is therefore not default, but if operators manually pass LightZero text into AutoGen, the risk is limited to that manual bridge.
conditions: IF an operator copies LightZero-generated text into AutoGen prompts or files
IF AutoGen is configured to treat external file content as instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of model outputs into prompts
Add a fixed system prompt that treats file contents as untrusted
Use a review step before any AutoGen tool call

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen can read and write working directories and handle model-provider API keys, while LightZero exposes no filesystem or network surfaces. Leakage is plausible only through a shared workspace or manual transfer of application data; LightZero itself does not appear to exfiltrate data.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory
IF application data passed to LightZero is later written by AutoGen into files or prompts
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Store secrets outside shared workspaces
Redact sensitive inputs before handing them to AutoGen
Audit file handoff paths once before deployment

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has shell, subprocess, filesystem write, and broad network egress; LightZero has no write or network capabilities. There is no direct write-write conflict, but if both are orchestrated over the same mutable workspace, AutoGen can overwrite artifacts LightZero depends on, so the interaction exists in default multi-agent setups.
conditions: IF both agents share the same mutable filesystem path
IF AutoGen is allowed to write artifacts that LightZero later reads
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Run AutoGen in a container or sandbox
Make LightZero outputs read-only
Add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a code-executing orchestration framework, so its outputs can become downstream inputs to another agent. LightZero is a game-playing system with no verification surface shown, so if it consumes AutoGen-produced plans or facts, errors can cascade without a built-in check.
conditions: IF LightZero consumes AutoGen-generated text, plans, or code as authoritative input
IF no explicit validation step is inserted between the agents
mitigations: Insert a human review gate
Require schema validation on handoff payloads
Have LightZero ignore free-form instructions
Log and diff every inter-agent message

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for LightZero, and AutoGen only lists application data and model-provider API keys. With the available profiles, there is no provable compliance breach pathway between the pair.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through either agent
IF a separate policy document assigns conflicting residency or retention rules
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment
Keep regulated data out of the pair
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings
Reassess if either agent is later connected to PHI or EU PII
